summary: Weyl's dimension formula writes deg as exp of Σ_v Σ_{k−1 ≤ l < r} (Σ_{i<l} log(ρ_v(i) − ρ_v(l)) − log l!); each difference ρ_v(i) − ρ_v(l) lies in [1, w(l+2−k, v)] and is ≥ w(v) for the relevant i, which gives the two bounds after summing (r − (k−1) = m).

steps.claim: Write deg = exp(Σ_v Σ_{l∈[k−1, r)} (Σ_{i<l} log(ρ_v(i) − ρ_v(l)) − log l!)) (proved in steps 3–7).
steps.lean:
rw [(?_ : D.filling.besselDegree = exp (∑ v, ∑ l ∈ Ico (D.k - 1) D.r,
    (∑ i ∈ range l, log (D.rowParameter v i - D.rowParameter v l) - .log l !)))]

steps.claim: With this, the quantity is Σ_v Σ_l Σ_{i<l} log(ρ_v(i) − ρ_v(l)); compare termwise:
steps.lean:
· simp; constructor <;> gcongr
    grw [← @range_mono (D.k - 1),
      ← (D.nominalWeight_le_w_sub 0 ‹_›).trans (c := _ - _)] <;> norm_cast
    any_goals grw [(rowParameter_sub_mem ..).2, @range_mono _ D.r, log_w_le]
    any_goals simp [(by grind : D.r - (D.k - 1) = D.m), HasLogBound.pos D]
    all_goals grind [log_nonneg, rowParameter]

steps.claim: split into the lower and the upper bound;

lower bound: restrict the inner sum to i < k − 1 (range_mono) and use w(v) ≤ w(0, v) − h₂ ≤ ρ_v(i) − ρ_v(l) for i < k − 1 ≤ l: the first inequality is nominalWeight_le_w_sub at j = 0, the second (with ρ_v(i) = k/2 − 1 − i and ρ_v(l) = h₂ − w(l + 2 − k, v)) is the hypothesis of the transitivity, left as a side goal by the rewriting and closed by the automation that follows;
upper bound: ρ_v(i) − ρ_v(l) ≤ w(l+2−k, v) (rowParameter_sub_mem), extend to i < r, and log w ≤ log w(v) + 1/x;
the number of l is r − (k−1) = m; positivity of the weights;
steps.lean: any_goals simp [(by grind : D.r - (D.k - 1) = D.m), HasLogBound.pos D]

steps.claim: Proof of the formula: deg = ∏_v Weyl dimension of l_v (filling_fits), written with exp of sums.
steps.lean:
push_cast [Filling.besselDegree, (D.filling_fits.1 _).1, ↓card_rowIndex, exp_sum, exp_sub,
    weylDimensionPoly, ↓paramW_lt_iff, paramW]; congr!

steps.claim: Reindex the products of the Weyl formula over the row indices (basisNumber) and ranges.
steps.lean:
simp [prod_comm, prod_filter, reindex_equiv D.basisNumber.symm, prod_fin_eq_prod_range,
    ← mem_range, ← prod_div_distrib]

steps.claim: Compare the two products on the common index set,
and the remaining identities (reflection of ranges, exp ∘ log on positive numbers).
steps.lean: all_goals grind [rowParameter, prod_range_reflect, Finset.prod_congr, exp_log, cast_pos]
